summary: A transmon qubit is coupled to a high-overtone bulk acoustic resonator (HBAR) and reset via repeated iSWAP gates with different GHz-frequency acoustic modes, achieving residual excited-state population $\langle p \rangle = 8.3 \times 10^{-5}$ with 95% confidence interval $[0.027, 2.52] \times 10^{-4}$. This represents a 5–10× improvement over existing microwave-based schemes and demonstrates that phononic baths provide intrinsically colder, hardware-efficient resources for high-fidelity qubit initialization.
motivation: Standard passive cooling leaves transmon qubits with residual excited-state populations near 1%, limiting protocols that require repeated initialization or operate near noise limits, such as quantum error correction and dark-matter detection.
method: A superconducting transmon coupled to an HBAR via a piezoelectric dome is driven with AC Stark shifts to resonantly swap excitations between the qubit and different acoustic modes ($g \approx 2\pi \times 300$ kHz, iSWAP duration $\sim 0.5$ µs per gate, four gates total). The acoustic modes have intrinsically low thermal occupation (independently measured steady-state phonon population $\sim 10^{-4}$) and are separated by 12.6 MHz in frequency, enabling multimode entropy extraction without additional dissipation channels.
result: After four iSWAP gates, the qubit population saturates at the measured steady-state phonon population level ($p_4 = 8.3 \times 10^{-5}$), with saturation after three gates ($p_3 = 1.3 \times 10^{-4}$), consistent with master-equation simulations using measured parameters: $T_{\mathrm{bath}} = 45 \pm 4$ mK, $T_1 = 23.1 \pm 12.4$ µs, $T_\phi = 17.1 \pm 8.1$ µs. Reset duration is 3.4 µs.
